A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ContextAgent and ContextAgentBench. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, out-of-domain evaluations, component ablations, model-size comparisons and qualitative results in Section 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and adds missing-modality experiments and comparisons with additional proprietary reasoning models.

M1.justification: Both versions use proactive-oriented context extraction, persona information, reasoning-trace distillation, supervised fine-tuning and threshold-triggered tool execution. Describing the renamed threshold as user-adjustable does not establish a new algorithm or component.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation with visual or audio context missing, extending the tested input conditions. The 1,000-sample ContextAgentBench, 300-sample Lite benchmark, nine scenarios and twenty tools remain unchanged; Appendix A's examples do not establish additional dataset coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 2 adds SFT-P to the Lite baseline comparison for Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B. Table 4 adds GPT-o3, GPT-o4-mini and Claude Sonnet 4 to the OOD comparison. Its GPT-4o and GPT-3.5-Turbo results already appeared in v1 Table 6.

E3.justification: v1 Appendix A specifies one training epoch for ContextAgentBench, including OOD, and five for Lite; v2 Section 5.1 specifies five epochs generally. This changes the reported budget without establishing reruns. v2 also introduces inference-time modality removal; the newly stated 60/40 split is additional disclosure, not an established split change.

E4.justification: v2 adds a missing-vision/missing-audio sensitivity analysis in Table 3, but removes the detailed Lite persona, thought-trace and context-extraction ablations from v1 Table 9 and its Table 2 summary. Main-benchmark component ablations, OOD tests, model-size analyses, tool-chain analyses and qualitative cases remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Matched main, Lite, OOD, model-size and tool-chain result tables retain their numerical values. v2 adds SFT-P, missing-modality and newer-model results; for example, Table 4 reports F1 scores of 0.711 for GPT-o3 and 0.648 for ContextAgent. The Lite component-ablation entries in v1 Table 9 are removed.

T1.justification: The agent mapping, context representation, score-trigger rule and SFT dataset formulation remain mathematically equivalent. Renaming the threshold from TR to theta and explaining its adjustability introduce no new derivation or formal result; neither version supplies theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a sensory-context-aware proactive agent, its benchmark and improved proactive prediction/tool calling. The headline performance claims are unchanged; increasing the evaluated model count from ten to thirteen expands supporting evidence.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies thought-trace benefits as smaller under SFT, interprets missing vision as more damaging than missing audio, and attributes conservative detection behavior to prompting. It also discusses stronger reasoning models' potential benefits. The limitations concerning tool diversity and scenario coverage remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code/data repository link, explicitly states a 60/40 training/test split and provides five detailed dataset examples. Implementation details move into Section 5.1, but the batch size of 64 and explicit experimental trigger threshold of 3 disappear. The epoch specification also changes; hardware, optimizer and LoRA details remain.

R1.justification: The same 56 references and substantive positioning against reactive agents, existing proactive agents and prior benchmarks are retained. Related-work wording changes do not alter the claimed research gap.

P1.justification: v2 lightly edits the abstract and technical prose, renames Section 5.1 to Experimental Setup, moves implementation details there, replaces Appendix A with dataset examples and adds acknowledgments. The overall argument and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds a main-text Lite comparison table and tables for missing sensors and newer reasoning models. The former ablation summary and detailed Lite ablation table disappear, while main-benchmark ablations remain in renumbered Table 10. Figures and other tables are repositioned or resized, with modest diagram refinements rather than a wholesale redesign.

improvement.justification: Additional comparators, modality tests, dataset examples and access information improve coverage and usability. However, v2 removes the Lite ablation evidence while retaining claims based on it. Its new modality experiment is described as using Lite, yet Table 3's full-model accuracy is 0.888 versus 0.840 in the Lite results in Table 7. These benefits and losses in evidential clarity prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
